page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Start from tan(50° − 40°)
steps.margin_note: First mark. Work BACKWARDS from the answer: 50° − 40° is 10°, so write tan(50° − 40°) = tan10° and expand the left side.

recall.must_convey: That tan(50° − 40°) = tan10° is written and the tan(A−B) formula expanded on the left.
accept: fifty minus forty is ten so write tan of fifty minus forty equals tan ten and expand
start from the difference of the angles and use the tan A minus B formula
fifty minus forty ante ten, tan A minus B formula rasta

steps.why: The answer contains tan10°, and 10° is the difference of the two angles on the left. Starting from that observation is what makes the proof one line long.
common_mistakes: Trying to expand tan 50° and tan 40° separately.

steps.label: Simplify the denominator
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 40° is 90° − 50°, so tan40° is cot50° — and tan50° × cot50° is exactly 1, making the denominator 2.

recall.must_convey: That tan40° = cot50°, so tan50° tan40° = 1 and the denominator becomes 2, giving the result on cross-multiplying.
accept: tan forty is cot fifty so the product is one and the denominator is two, then cross multiply
the denominator becomes one plus one which is two
tan times cot is one so the bottom is two
tan forty ante cot fifty, product one, denominator two
cross multiplying gives two tan ten

steps.why: The 2 in the answer comes from 1 + 1 in the denominator. Everything else was already there — that single simplification is the whole proof.
common_mistakes: Not spotting that 40° and 50° are complementary.
Forgetting to cross-multiply at the end.
